label: Matt 8:1
text: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

label: Matt 8:2
text: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”

label: Matt 8:3
text:
Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying,
“I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

label: Matt 8:4
text:
Jesus said to him,
“See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

label: Matt 8:5
text: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him,

label: Matt 8:6
text: and saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”

label: Matt 8:7
text:
Jesus said to him,
“I will come and heal him.”

label: Matt 8:8
text: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

label: Matt 8:9
text: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

label: Matt 8:10
text:
When Jesus heard it, he marveled, and said to those who followed,
“Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

label: Matt 8:11
text: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,

label: Matt 8:12
text: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

label: Matt 8:13
text:
Jesus said to the centurion,
“Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.

label: Matt 8:14
text: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.

label: Matt 8:15
text: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.

label: Matt 8:16
text: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick;

label: Matt 8:17
text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”

label: Matt 8:18
text: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.

label: Matt 8:19
text: A scribe came, and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

label: Matt 8:20
text:
Jesus said to him,
“The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

label: Matt 8:21
text: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

label: Matt 8:22
text:
But Jesus said to him,
“Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”

label: Matt 8:23
text: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.

label: Matt 8:24
text: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.

label: Matt 8:25
text: They came to him, and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”

label: Matt 8:26
text:
He said to them,
“Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?”
 Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.

label: Matt 8:27
text: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

label: Matt 8:28
text:
When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes,
 two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' lists Γαδαρηνων (Gadarenes) in B (Vaticanus), also C, M, Θ, Σ, 174, 1010, ℓ 253 and versional fathers - the reading of most modern translations.
The article's named witnesses (minuscule 892c, Claromontanus Δ, the Latin tradition, Origen) are not manuscript nodes of this graph, so attested_by is left empty rather than inventing ids.
The article lists Γαζαρηνων (Gazarenes) in א* - the original hand of Sinaiticus; its corrector (א2) reads Gergesenes, the WEB reading of this passage.

label: Matt 8:29
text: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”

label: Matt 8:30
text: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.

label: Matt 8:31
text: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”

label: Matt 8:32
text:
He said to them,
“Go!”
They came out, and went into the herd of pigs: and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water.

label: Matt 8:33
text: Those who fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.

label: Matt 8:34
text: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.

label: Great crowds followed Jesus down from the mountain
statement: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

label: A leper came to Jesus asking to be made clean
statement: A leper came to Jesus and worshiped him, saying that he could make him clean if he wanted to.

label: Jesus touched the leper and cleansed him
statement: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the leper, and the leprosy was cleansed.

label: The cleansed leper's offering that Moses commanded
statement: The cleansed leper was to tell nobody, show himself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony.

label: A centurion came to Jesus at Capernaum
statement: When Jesus came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him asking for his paralyzed servant.

label: The centurion commanded soldiers under authority
statement: The centurion was a man under authority with soldiers under himself, saying to one 'Go' and he goes, to another 'Come' and he comes.

label: Reclining at the banquet of the Kingdom with the patriarchs
statement: Many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven.

label: Peter's mother-in-law sick with fever in Peter's house
statement: When Jesus came into Peter's house in Capernaum, he saw his wife's mother lying sick with a fever; he touched her hand, the fever left her, and she got up and served him.

label: Many possessed with demons brought to Jesus at evening
statement: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick.

label: Matthew quotes Isaiah on taking our infirmities
statement: Matthew quotes Isaiah the prophet: 'He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.'

label: Foxes have holes and birds have nests
statement: Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.

label: Burying a father as a duty delaying discipleship
statement: A disciple asked to go first and bury his father; Jesus said to follow him and leave the dead to bury their own dead.

label: Jesus and his disciples crossed the sea in a boat
statement: Jesus got into a boat and his disciples followed him across the sea.

label: A violent storm suddenly came up on the sea
statement: A violent storm came up on the sea so suddenly that the boat was covered with the waves.

label: Crossing to the other side into the Gadarene/Gergesene country
statement: Jesus came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gergesenes (Gadarenes in most translations; the manuscripts differ).
note: Manuscripts differ: Gadarenes, Gerasenes or Gergesenes; the location is disputed (Gadara, Gerasa or Kursi).

label: Demoniacs coming out of the tombs
statement: Two men possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, so fierce that nobody could pass that way.

label: A herd of many pigs feeding near the tombs
statement: A herd of many pigs was feeding far away from them.

label: The herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea
statement: The demons entered the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the water.

label: The whole city begged Jesus to depart
statement: The whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him, they begged him to depart from their borders.

label: Wikipedia: Akeldama (Tomb of the Shroud, leprosy DNA)
title: Akeldama
excerpt: The Tomb of the Shroud in Akeldama is "one of very few examples of a preserved shrouded human burial" dating to the first century, with the bone samples yielding evidence of the pathogens Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium leprae

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Gergesenes variant)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: The King James Version in ( Matthew 8:28 ) has the location as "Gergesenes" which corresponds to the modern Kursi , although this identification is disputed since Gergasa is not known to have existed prior to late antiquity nor does it appear in early manuscripts.

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (location dispute)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: The exact location of the miracle is a matter of dispute, with the Gospels themselves only indicating a general area where the miracle took place.

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Gadara off the shore)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: The story appears to be set close to the Sea of Galilee, since it takes place as soon as Jesus gets out of the boat, but neither Gadara nor Gerasa is on the shore itself.

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Decapolis, minimal Jewish presence)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: Historically, the cities of the Decapolis were outside of the territory of Roman province of Judaea and had a minimal Jewish presence during the time period of Jesus's ministry.

label: Wikipedia: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac (Hippos speculated)
title: Exorcism of the Gerasene demoniac
excerpt: Some modern scholars have also speculated that Hippos (Golan Heights) , located within Israel's pre- 1967 borders could be a potential location for the exorcism due to its proximity to the coast of the Sea of Galilee.

label: Wikipedia: Umm Qais (Gadara joins the Decapolis)
title: Umm Qais
excerpt: In 63 BCE , Roman general Pompey conquered the region, Gadara was rebuilt and became a member of the semi-autonomous Roman Decapolis .

label: Wikipedia: Umm Qais (tombs still visible)
title: Umm Qais
excerpt: In 1806 Ulrich Jasper Seetzen visited Umm Qais and identified it as the location of ancient Gadara, describing the Ottoman settlement and the tombs and other monuments still visible on the surface.

label: Wikipedia: Kursi, Sea of Galilee (traditional identification)
title: Kursi, Sea of Galilee
excerpt: The site contains the remains of a Byzantine monastery and is traditionally identified as the location of Jesus' "Miracle of the Swine".

label: Wikipedia: Kursi, Sea of Galilee (excavation)
title: Kursi, Sea of Galilee
excerpt: Major excavation took place between 1971 and 1974 headed by Israeli archaeologist Dan Urman [ 8 ] and his Greek colleague Vassilios Tzaferis [ 1 ] for the Israel Antiquities Authority

label: Wikipedia: Calming the storm (sudden storms on the lake)
title: Calming the storm
excerpt: Author Michael Keene commented that the Sea of Galilee was known for its sudden and fierce storms and that the Jews were people of the land who were generally uncomfortable at sea

label: Wikipedia: Red fox (burrows and dens)
title: Red fox
excerpt: Their burrows are often dug on hill or mountain slopes, in ravines and on steep riverbanks, as well as in ditches, depressions and gutters, and in rock clefts and neglected human environments.

label: Wikipedia: Red fox (summary, range)
title: Red fox (REST summary)
excerpt: The red fox is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora. It is present across the entire Northern Hemisphere, including most of Europe, Asia, and North America, as well as parts of North Africa.

label: Wikipedia: Ossuary (Second Temple secondary burial)
title: Ossuary
excerpt: During the Second Temple period , Jewish burial customs were varied, differing based on class and belief. For the wealthy, [ 3 ] one option available included primary burials in burial caves, followed by secondary burials in ossuaries

label: Wikipedia: Matthew 8:5 (centurion rank and garrison question)
title: Matthew 8:5
excerpt: Centurion was a rank in the Roman Army, low level officer in command of 100 infantry. At the time the area was ruled by Herod Antipas , not directly under Roman rule, so one question is why a Roman Centurian would be present.

label: Wikipedia: Matthew 8:5 (Gundry's three possibilities)
title: Matthew 8:5
excerpt: New Testament scholar Robert Gundry presents three possibilities: as a border town there may still well have been a Roman garrison; the Centurion may have travelled from a directly administered region like Roman Syria ; or Herod's forces may have used ranks similar to the Roman army

label: Wikipedia: Religious restrictions on the consumption of pork (Roman period)
title: Religious restrictions on the consumption of pork
excerpt: During the Roman period , abstinence from pork became one of the most identifiable features of the Jewish religion to outsiders.

label: Wikipedia: Religious restrictions on the consumption of pork (pig-bone assumptions)
title: Religious restrictions on the consumption of pork
excerpt: It was previously thought that an absence of pig remains at archaeological sites were indicative of Israelite ethnic presence, but research has challenged past assumptions.
